conventions.statement_de: Ein Hut bedeutet immer einen Operator, Â; der Strich der Ket-Notation einen Vektor, |ψ⟩; ein Symbol ohne Verzierung eine Zahl. Ausnahmen (TJO, 2026-10-29): der Einsoperator 𝕀, Zustände (Dichteoperatoren ρ, auch ein reiner Zustand als Operator geschrieben), die Pauli-Matrizen σ_j und Ket-Bras |a⟩⟨b| tragen keinen Hut.
conventions.statement_en: A hat always means an operator, Â; the bar of the ket notation a vector, |ψ⟩; a symbol without decoration a number. Exceptions (TJO, 2026-10-29): the identity operator 𝕀, states (density operators ρ, also a pure state written as an operator), the Pauli matrices σ_j and ket-bras |a⟩⟨b| carry no hat.

conventions.notes: Decision D-HAT, TJO 2026-10-29: hats on operators throughout course and script, revised the same day: four exceptions, namely the identity 𝕀, states (density operators ρ and pure states written as operators), the Pauli matrices σ_j and ket-bras |a⟩⟨b| (TJO: "definitely no hats for bra kets"), all without a hat. Effects, Hamiltonians, unitaries, projectors and other operators keep the hat. The macro is \op{A} (sym.operator-hat). A bare 0 would not show whether an operator, a number or a vector is meant, hence \Nul (sym.null-operator).
